To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a CRISPRi screening system for yeast that allows for chemical-genetic interaction discovery, and we identified generalizable features of guide RNAs that are important for effective transcriptional repression.
the best gRNAs in yeast are those that target low nucleosome occupancy regions and that are located between the transcription start sites (TSSs) and 200 base pairs upstream of the TSTs.

we developed a new inducible CRISPRi plasmid for yeast, we used this system to perform genome-scale CRISPRi screens in the presence of small molecule treatments, and we determined rules for guide RNA efficacy based on chromatin state and target position.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of CRISPRi as a powerful functional genomics tool, with a particular emphasis on defining the features of effective gRNAs in yeast.
the development and application of CRISPR-based genome editing tools for functional genomic and chemical genomics studies in the yeast model eukaryote.
the development of a CRISPRi-based functional genomics platform in S. cerevisiae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our study establishes a powerful functional and chemogenomics screening method and provides guidelines for designing effective guide RNAs that consider chromatin state, position relative to the transcription start site and length of the guide RNA.
we have established a powerful functional and chemogenomic screening method and provide general guidelines for designing effective guides.

the CRISPR interference system in yeast is an extremely powerful tool for studying gene function in a variety of contexts, and the rules for guide RNA selection and design that are presented here will enable researchers to maximize the utility of this system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rules we have identified for gRNA design in yeast will likely be generalizable to other organisms.
CRISPRi can be used for functional genomics in yeast and that the best guide RNAs are those that are located in the open chromatin region and close to the TSS.

the CRISPR interference system is a powerful functional genomics method, which can be used in yeast to identify genes that are essential to the cell in the presence of a drug or other stressor, and to determine rules for guide RNA efficacy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best region for targeting gRNAs is the promoter region, between the transcription start and 200 basepairs upstream of it.

the most effective gRNA targets are located between 200 and 500 bp upstream of a gene's TSS, and that the specificity of truncated (18 nt) gRNAs is not clearly superior in yeast to the specificity of full-length (20 nt) gRNA.
the rules for gRNA design are different in yeast and human cells, and that the most important factor is to target a region of low nucleosome occupancy, which is generally upstream of the TATA box.
